# Tinct: guide for AI crawlers

Tinct is a reader for public-domain classics: a modern English edition beside the original text, AI help for any passage, audio narration, notes, highlights and reading progress.

## Public pages

- `/read/{book}`: the book page. For a book with a modern English edition it opens on the first chapter (or the first scene of a play) in modern English, with the original text in the same page, the book's structure (for example "38 chapters" or "5 acts · 20 scenes") and the list of every chapter.
- `/read/{book}/chapter-N`: one page per chapter, the whole chapter in modern English with the original in the same page. Chapter 1's canonical address is the book page.
- `/read/{play}/act-N-scene-M`: one page per scene for Hamlet, Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet, Julius Caesar and Othello. The first scene's canonical address is the play's book page.
- `/modern-english`: every book with a modern English edition, grouped by shelf.
- `/read/shelf/{shelf}`: the books on one library shelf.
- `/read`: the library.

## How the editions are made

Tinct's modern English is drafted with AI from a public-domain translation (named on each book page, with its year) or from the author's original English text, then checked by a separate AI review against that source. The original is one tap away on every page.

Robots policy: public HTML pages are intended for indexing and citation. `/data/`, `/api/` and `/audio/` are not intended for crawling or bulk extraction.
